meta.title: Mortgage application states
meta.description: The states a home loan application passes through, with the property valuation and the legal checks running at the same time.

summary.headline: After approval in principle, the valuation and the legal checks run in parallel, and the lender issues an offer only when both are done.
points: Automated credit and fraud checks decline some applications before an underwriter sees them.
Underwriters can ask for more documents without moving the application on.
Valuation and conveyancing are regions of one Property checks state: both are active at once.
An offer that is not completed within six months expires.

facts.States: 9 plus a check, fork, join, start and end

data.title: Start
data.description: A broker or the applicant starts an application online.

data.title: Submitted
data.subtitle: Income and property details in
data.description: The application, payslips, bank statements and the property address are all in.

data.title: Credit and fraud checks pass?
data.description: A credit reference search, an identity check and fraud scoring run automatically within minutes.

data.title: Underwriting
data.subtitle: Affordability assessed
data.description: An underwriter checks income, outgoings and stress-tested repayments against the lending policy.

data.title: Fork
data.description: Starts the valuation and the legal work at the same time.

data.title: Property valued
data.subtitle: Report received
data.description: The surveyor's figure must support the loan-to-value the applicant asked for.

data.title: Searches ordered
data.subtitle: Local authority and title
data.description: The conveyancer orders local authority, drainage and environmental searches.

data.title: Join
data.description: Waits for both the valuation report and the certificate of title.

data.title: Completed
data.subtitle: Funds released
data.description: The money goes to the conveyancer on completion day and the loan account opens.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: An application is checked, underwritten, then split into two pieces of work that run at once: valuing the property and the legal checks. The offer waits for both.

steps.title: Submission and automated checks
steps.description: Once the documents are in, credit, identity and fraud checks run automatically. A failure declines the application before an underwriter spends time on it.

steps.title: Underwriting
steps.description: The underwriter may ask for more payslips or an explanation of a large payment; the application stays in Underwriting (the loop). It ends either in approval in principle or a decline on affordability.

steps.title: Valuation and legal work at once
steps.description: The fork starts both regions. A surveyor visits the house while the applicant's conveyancer orders searches and checks the title; neither waits for the other.

steps.title: The offer waits for both
steps.description: The join fires only when the valuation report and the certificate of title are both in. Then the formal offer is issued.

steps.title: Completion or expiry
steps.description: On completion day the funds go to the conveyancer and the loan starts. An offer not used within six months expires, and declined applications close straight away.
